role: retrospective finite-library fixed-budget search and independent-stream finite-window verification replay; not prospective confirmation
registration_context: All source and 2024 outcomes observed, frozen design coverage 3/3 versus 1/3 already known. Rules fixed now before replay random-stream outcomes; no outcome-blind efficacy claim.
continuation: Common outcome-free uniform full-library permutation with each arm observed initial IDs skipped; three distinct remaining library candidates. Explicit finite-library continuation adaptation, not arbitrary continuous Sobol policies.
search: One uniform window draw with replacement per candidate; same index stream in both arms. Observations consist of success indicator and cost only on success.
shortlist: Successful observations ordered by finite cost then evaluation index; failures after successful observations, in evaluation order, with cost null. No penalized objective, conditional population mean estimate, safety margin or fictitious failed cost.
verification: Freeze shortlist before fresh independent uniform-start streams with replacement. Execute represented 80 trials per attempted candidate, no within-candidate early stop. Certificate requires all success and exact one-sided Clopper-Pearson lower bound >=.95 with delta=.05/3; stop at first certificate, otherwise abstain. Repeated starts remain separate iid draw records.
truth: Only after replay decision use saved complete finite-population success counts; null full-population objective unless every window succeeds. No truth-based candidate selection.
accounting: Cache replay performs zero new controller calls, not 7590 physical evaluations. Report represented per-run search/verification queries separately, source archive 44968 paid once. Average repeats within each seasonal task then sum three tasks; no fictional M=20 or independent-repeat deployment interpretation.
limitations: Retrospective analyst-designed announced simulation, overlapping finite windows in one market, previously observed target outcomes. Independent random streams certify only the fixed uniform-window empirical law, not independent calendar periods or real operation. This tests source first-center adaptation, not full augmented atlas or Bayesian optimizer. Represented query comparisons omit unequal runtimes; archive actual acquisition/calls remain explicit.
